title: Best TCL Dehumidifier (2026): Reviews of Every Current Model
dek: Better known for TVs, TCL builds its dehumidifiers in a factory it co-owns with De'Longhi. Here's how to read its tangle of model numbers and pick the right one.
description: Our TCL dehumidifier review covers the 20, 40, 50 and 70-pint models, the smart pump unit, the De'Longhi factory link and how to decode TCL model numbers.
intro: This TCL dehumidifier review starts with a surprise: the brand you know from televisions has been building dehumidifiers for two decades. In 2005, TCL and Italy's De'Longhi Group set up a joint venture, **TCL-De'Longhi Home Appliances**, in Zhongshan, China, specifically to make dehumidifiers and portable air conditioners for both companies. A TCL unit and a De'Longhi unit can come off the same production lines wearing different logos.

That background explains why TCL's build quality lands close to De'Longhi's — and the shopping headache is model numbers. TCL currently sells overlapping lineups under at least four naming schemes depending on the retailer: TDW, DEA, D91 and H-series. Two listings that both say "50-pint" can be different hardware generations.

We sorted through the current lineup using TCL's spec sheets, retailer listings, published third-party reviews and owner feedback. Here are the four TCL dehumidifiers worth your attention, and how to make sure you're buying the one you think you are.
topPicksLead: For a bedroom or small-to-mid room, the **TCL 20-Pint (TDW20E20)** is the best overall: quiet, simple and rated for about 1,500 sq ft.

products.name: TCL 20-Pint Dehumidifier (TDW20E20)
pros: Rated as low as 49 dB on its lowest fan speed
Casters make it easy to move between rooms
cons: 7.4-pint bucket needs regular emptying in damp rooms
products.whyWeLoveIt: Most people shopping TCL want something affordable and unfussy for a bedroom, office or laundry room. The TDW20E20 nails that brief with a real set-a-number humidistat and a quiet low setting that won't keep you up at night.
products.performance: TCL rates it for roughly 1,500 sq ft, which matches a damp bedroom or small living space rather than a basement. The 7.4-pint bucket shuts the unit off when full, so it fails safe, but in a muggy room you'll be emptying it daily. Consumer Reports has evaluated this model, and owner reviews generally describe it as a quiet, dependable single-room machine. If price is your top concern, compare it with the field in our [best budget dehumidifier](/best/best-budget-dehumidifier/) guide.
products.notes: One retailer listing title claims 2,000 sq ft for this model; TCL's own spec sheet says about 1,500. Trust the spec sheet.

products.name: TCL 40-Pint Dehumidifier (TDW40E20)
pros: Consumer Reports rated it very good overall
cons: Bulkier than the 20-pint for a bedroom
products.whyWeLoveIt: The 40-pint steps up to a living room or a modest basement without much extra cost. Auto-restart is an underrated feature: if a summer storm knocks out power, it picks up where it left off instead of sitting idle.
products.performance: TCL rates it for about 3,500 sq ft, and its 14-pint bucket takes roughly nine hours to fill at full rated output — enough to get through a workday. It's one of the few TCL models with a published independent lab evaluation, with Consumer Reports giving it a very good overall score. Frost control helps in a basement that runs in the low 60s. See how it stacks up in our [best dehumidifier for basement](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) roundup.

products.name: TCL 50-Pint Smart Dehumidifier with Pump (H50D26W)
products.award: Best smart pick with a pump
pros: App control plus basement, bedroom and continuous presets
Highest coverage rating in the lineup
cons: Shares a confusing H-series name with the H50D44W
products.whyWeLoveIt: This is the TCL to buy if you never want to carry a bucket again. The pump sends water to a sink or out a window through a 16-foot hose, and the app lets you check on a basement from upstairs.
products.performance: TCL rates it for up to 4,500 sq ft — more than its own 70-pint model — and the 41°F operating floor suits a cool basement or attached garage. The preset modes take the guesswork out of choosing a target humidity. Owners value the hands-off drainage most, which is exactly why it exists. Compare it with other self-draining units in our [best dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.
products.notes: Prices for this model differ noticeably between retailers, so cross-check before you buy.

products.name: TCL 70-Pint Dehumidifier (DEA70E)
pros: Highest pints-per-day rating in the lineup
cons: Lower coverage rating than the 50-pint pump model
products.whyWeLoveIt: For a wet, unfinished basement where you want the most water pulled per day, the DEA70E is TCL's heavy hitter. Auto-defrost keeps it working when the space is cool.
products.performance: Here's the quirk: TCL rates the 70-pint for about 3,000 sq ft, less than the 50-pint H50D26W. Coverage figures depend on how each listing was written, so don't assume bigger pints always means more floor space. Where it shines is moisture load — a soggy basement that needs heavy extraction, not a big dry one. A pump version (sold as DEA70EP or TDW70EPB19) adds continuous drainage. For more high-capacity options see our [best dehumidifier for large room](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-large-room/) picks.

sections.heading: How we pick the best TCL dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We don't lab-test. For this guide we compared TCL's own spec sheets against retailer listings (and flagged where they disagree), checked the CPSC database for recalls, reviewed published independent evaluations such as Consumer Reports' scores, and read owner reviews for recurring faults like leaking buckets, noisy compressors and failed pumps.
Because TCL's naming is so tangled, we only recommend specific model numbers we could match to a TCL spec sheet. That's also why you won't see a generic "TCL 50-pint" on our list.

sections.heading: What to look for in a TCL dehumidifier

items.label: The exact model number
items.text: Match TDW, DEA, D91 or H-series codes, not just the pint rating, before comparing prices across stores.

items.label: Coverage from TCL, not a listing title
items.text: Retailer titles sometimes inflate square footage. Check TCL's spec sheet, and use our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) to sanity-check.

items.label: Drainage that suits the room
items.text: A bucket is fine for a bedroom. For a basement you don't visit daily, choose the H50D26W or the 70-pint pump version.

items.label: Cold-room features
items.text: If the space drops into the 50s or low 60s, look for auto-defrost or frost control and a 41°F operating rating.

items.label: Smart features you'll use
items.text: The D91 and H-series add app control; worth it for basements, less so for a bedroom unit you walk past every day.

sections.heading: TCL smart dehumidifiers and other model lines, decoded

items: **TDW-series** (TDW20E20, TDW40E20, TDW70EPB19): the core lineup, sold widely and direct from TCL.
**DEA-series** (DEA70E, DEA70EP): appears at some retailers for the same 70-pint class under a different code.
**D91 "Smart" series** (20D91, 50D91-B): TCL's connected tier, adding Wi-Fi app and voice-assistant control.
**H-series** (H50D26W, H50D44W): carried mainly by big-box home stores, pump-equipped and app-connected.

blocks.text: Several of these overlap in capacity but aren't necessarily identical inside. The **H50D44W**, for example, is a sibling of our H50D26W pick; if you're considering it, compare its spec sheet line by line for coverage, pump lift and operating temperature rather than assuming they're the same machine.

sections.heading: Is TCL a good dehumidifier brand? The De'Longhi connection

blocks.text: TCL's dehumidifiers come from a factory it co-owns with De'Longhi, which is a closer relationship than the typical arrangement where one manufacturer builds finished units for unrelated brands. Engineering, compressor sourcing and quality control can be shared, so the real differences between a TCL and a De'Longhi are often price, features and warranty rather than build. Compare the Italian side of the family in our [best De'Longhi dehumidifier](/best/best-delonghi-dehumidifier/) guide.

blocks.title: Recall check
blocks.text: We found no CPSC recall tied to the TCL dehumidifier name as of this update — a cleaner record than the many brands caught up in the 2021 New Widetech recall. Still, search your exact model number at CPSC.gov before buying used.

The **TCL 20-Pint (TDW20E20)** is the best TCL dehumidifier for a bedroom or small room, and the **TDW40E20** steps up to a living room or basement with a strong independent score. If you're done hauling buckets, the **H50D26W** smart pump model is the one to get, while the **DEA70E** brings the most extraction to a wet basement. Whatever you choose, match the exact model number and trust TCL's spec sheet over listing titles. For the wider field, see our [best dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier/) picks.

faqs.q: What is the best TCL dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For a bedroom or small room, the TCL 20-Pint (TDW20E20), rated for about 1,500 sq ft. For a larger living area or basement, the TDW40E20 covers about 3,500 sq ft. If you want a built-in pump and app control, choose the H50D26W, rated up to 4,500 sq ft.

Mostly, yes. Consumer Reports rated the TDW40E20 very good overall, and owner reviews generally describe TCL units as quiet, simple and good value. Common complaints are the one-year warranty and small buckets on the non-pump models.

They're built by TCL-De'Longhi Home Appliances in Zhongshan, China, a joint venture TCL formed with Italy's De'Longhi Group in 2005 to make dehumidifiers and portable air conditioners for both brands.

faqs.q: What is a TCL smart dehumidifier?
faqs.a: TCL's smart models — the D91 series and pump-equipped H-series such as the H50D26W and H50D44W — add Wi-Fi app control so you can set humidity, switch modes and check status from your phone. Some also work with voice assistants.

faqs.q: What does E3 mean on a TCL dehumidifier?
faqs.a: E-codes on TCL units generally point to a sensor or component fault, and the exact meaning varies by model. Unplug the unit for a few minutes, restart it, and check the error table in your manual. If the code returns, contact TCL support, especially while the unit is under warranty.

faqs.q: Does a bigger pint rating mean a TCL covers more space?
faqs.a: Not always. TCL rates its 70-pint DEA70E for about 3,000 sq ft but its 50-pint H50D26W for up to 4,500 sq ft. Use the coverage figure on TCL's spec sheet, and size up for very damp spaces.
